content.comment_body: Hello! Last week, I got a new laptop running Windows 7. I re-installed [product_name] V6 that I used on my old laptop and updated it to V7 (English). Now, when trying to use it for the first time with a [product_name] [article_no] via USB connection, I ran into a problem: I can't connect to the device. I attached a screenshot showing the error. I already downloaded and installed the USB drivers from [company_name]'s website. When I try 'auto detect' in the user interface, nothing is detected. I've confirmed that the selected module version is correct and even tried another option, but the same issue remains. Is it possible that I need to change the COM port configuration in my PC settings? If so, how is this done? Thanks, [user_name]

Is your Windows 7 installation 64-bit or 32-bit? Also, check if Java is installed via Control Panel (especially since you upgraded). [product_name] often looks at the first four COM ports, so if your laptop previously had devices like Bluetooth, check Device Manager and assign the relevant device to one of the first four COM ports. You might find this [url] useful. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue involves connecting a [company_name] automation device to a Windows 7 laptop using [product_name] software over USB. Despite installing the correct drivers and software versions, the auto-detect function does not find the device. Community advice points to checking Java installation and adjusting COM port assignments to resolve compatibility and detection problems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects straightforward connectivity between their laptop and the automation device via USB, with software auto-detection working reliably after proper installation.
